narrative.overview: DocWriter is a harbour at night lit by one lamp. Fog by day, lamplight after dark: sea-glass neutrals, a single verdigris accent, and a serif that belongs to the manuscript rather than the software. The system is quiet, salt-worn and lamplit — it never decorates, it only holds light on the thing being worked on. The visual language splits the labour: Spectral carries everything the writer named, Hanken Grotesk carries the apparatus, and DM Mono labels the small print. Three light conditions are first-class: Fog, Harbor night and Driftwood.
keyCharacteristics: Sea-glass neutrals with one verdigris accent per screen.
Spectral for names and prose, Hanken Grotesk for controls, DM Mono for labels and counts.
Softly tactile surfaces: 20px cards, 1px top light, layered downward shadows.
Colour as data: five type hues identify entity kinds, never decoration.
Density is a multiplier (--density), not a second layout.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: The accent marks the active or primary thing and nothing else. On any screen it covers well under a tenth of the pixels; its scarcity is what makes it read as light.

rules.name: The Type-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Entity hues come from the types table. Never hard-code a type colour in a component, and never reassign a hue for decoration — the reader learns the five colours as a key.

rules.name: The Three Lights Rule
rules.body: A surface is finished only when it is legible in Fog, Harbor night and Driftwood. Never ship a component with a hard-coded background or text hex; bind it to a --color-* token.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Spectral is for what the writer named or reads; Hanken is for what the software does. A button never uses the serif, and a chapter title never uses the grotesk.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: Functional text never goes below 11px. Group heads sit one step above at 12px; every other mono label, count and badge is 11px.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose never exceeds 660px. The 1000px Bible column is for scanning cards, not for reading sentences.

rules.name: The One Multiplier Rule
rules.body: New spacing uses calc(Npx * var(--density)). A fixed height that ignores the multiplier breaks compact mode.

rules.name: The Top-Light Rule
rules.body: If a surface is raised, it carries an inset top highlight. A shadow without the inset light reads as a sticker.

rules.name: The Four Shadows Rule
rules.body: Depth uses these four tokens only. A new component composes them; it does not invent a fifth.

rules.name: The Soft Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius scales with the size of the thing. A 20px radius on a 34px chip looks like a mistake; a 9px radius on a panel looks unfinished.

dos: Do use the accent for one thing per screen: the active chip, the primary button, the focus ring.
Do bind entity colour through the inline --e property sourced from the type row.
Do check every screen in Fog, Harbor night and Driftwood before calling it done.
Do keep raised surfaces on the four shadow tokens with the 1px inset highlight.
Do multiply spacing by --density so compact mode keeps working.
Do use --color-text-secondary for placeholders and empty text; it clears AA on every theme.
donts: Don't add a second accent hue, a gradient hero, or a metric-tile row. The rejected reference is the generic SaaS dashboard.
Don't hard-code type or theme hex values inside a component.
Don't use --color-text-faint for functional text — it measures 3.9:1 at night.
Don't use DM Mono for anything longer than a label.
Don't use pure-black shadows or a fifth elevation.
Don't fix a card or control height that ignores the density multiplier.
